question: Do fully-trained conventional recurrent and empirical model-based controllers extract paid-action consequences from the same MD30 physical observations and provide a credible baseline for any future native non-token candidate?

cohorts.training_evidence: Each episode's 8 physically charged World.step receipts, 4 per stage, no hidden graph access
cohorts.eval_evidence: Each control obtains a separate real World.step episode with up to 3 diagnostics per stage; no counterfactual oracle access
cohorts.holdout_usage: Fixed single diagnostic-only toy transfer readout, no post-score hyperparameter changes

recurrent.method: Conventional Elman tanh RNN world-model with fully trained input/recurrent/output weights, sequence cross-entropy optimized by full 8-step backpropagation through time and Adam
recurrent.input_features: One-hot action (8), last public sensor vector (6), current public phase one-hot (2), where stage reset ambient sensor is explicitly observed
recurrent.train_order: Seeded epoch shuffles, exact original charge-order within episodes; no teacher hidden graph or uncharged physical actions
recurrent.loss: Six-bit next-observation BCE mean over time, episodes and six target bits
recurrent.checkpoint: Save validation-best network weights, epoch, val BCE, parameter counts and consumed physical trace hash
recurrent.planning: Model predicts physical effects of each available actuator and diagnostic from its own learned hidden state; one-step estimated diagnostic information-value heuristic, then reselect after each paid observation
recurrent.probe_threshold: Best actuator expected target probability < 0.68 AND predicted diagnostic Bernoulli entropy > 0.75; no probe if unavailable
recurrent.convergence_rule: Report train and validation BCE, epoch, patience and whether validation stabilized; do not call fully qualified strong baseline if validation fails or undertrains

model_based_rl.method: Conventional empirical action-conditioned MDP learned from paid public sensor transitions with smoothed backoff; explicit Bellman action-value lookahead and diagnostic value-of-information
model_based_rl.state: (public phase, C,D,E,F sensor bits) plus spent-probe count
model_based_rl.actions: Available actuator intervention A/B to value=1; internal diagnostics C/D/E to 0 or 1
model_based_rl.transition: Fit empirical categorical distribution over full six-bit observed next sensor vectors by (phase,last CDEF bits,action), fallback to (phase,action); Laplace prior smoothing
model_based_rl.train_splits: Only 192 fit episodes update transition/reward counts; 48 validation episodes for logloss report
model_based_rl.reward: Diagnostic -0.05, actuator +0.98 if target F=1 otherwise -0.52; all derived from paid receipts
model_based_rl.planning: One-step Bellman lookahead with expected distributional sensor updates and follow-up actuator selection; diagnostic cost charged, at most one planned diagnostic per stage to prevent free repeated adaptation
model_based_rl.convergence_rule: Report fitted observed state-action cells, coverage, training/validation negative log likelihood; fail closed on empty transition statistics or nonfinite values

fairness.comparison: Run Bayesian existing + the two new controls on same physical data seed set; compare to fixed blind only as synthetic engineering diagnostic; strongest model benchmark remains UNVERIFIED
fairness.compute: Record training CPU seconds and decision CPU seconds for each; do not claim comparable accuracy at matched compute without measured normalization
fairness.public_interface: Only World.observe() and World.step() with charged histories, no read of world private graph, no future labels, no official seed use

stop.infra: Any focusing/inherited test, code atlas, dual-OS parity or source custody failure -> ENGINEERING_FAIL, no promotion
stop.science: A toy transfer result alone is exploratory even with positive numbers; preserve negative or failed baselines, do not tune protocol based on outcomes
stop.deployment: No branch merge, accepted ref, main, native weights, owner controller, runner, scheduled tasks, or actual model learning claim
